cards.text: Some of the disciples are admiring the temple in Jerusalem: the beautiful stones, the gifts given to God. They're like tourists who took forty pictures of one wall and are going for forty-one. Then Jesus, God's Son, speaks up about those stones.

cards.question: The disciples are admiring the temple's beautiful stones. What does Jesus say will happen to those stones?

answers.text: Not one will be left on another
They will last a thousand years
They will all be covered in gold

cards.text: Every stone? Thrown DOWN? I bet the disciples are stunned. They call Him Teacher and ask Him two questions.

cards.question: Jesus just said the temple's stones will be thrown down. What two things do the disciples ask Him?

answers.text: When it will happen and what the sign will be
Who will do it and how they can stop it
Why it must happen and where they should go

cards.text: No date, and nobody gets a calendar invite. Instead Jesus warns that many will come in His name, claiming, 'I am He,' and, 'The time is near.'

cards.question: Because of those people coming in His name, Jesus tells the disciples to see to it that they are not ___.
Jesus tells the disciples it's fine to follow the people who come saying, 'The time is near.'

cards.text: Next up, scary news: wars and rebellions. Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer panicking every time it rattled, so I am listening VERY closely to this part.

cards.question: When the disciples hear of wars and rebellions, what does Jesus tell them?
Jesus says that wars and rebellions mean the end is coming right away.

cards.text: Jesus keeps going: 'Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom.' He isn't softening any of it.

cards.question: Nation against nation, kingdom against kingdom. What else does Jesus say there will be in various places?
Along with fearful sights, Jesus says there will be great ___ from heaven.

cards.text: Then Jesus turns from the whole world to the disciples right in front of Him. And He talks about timing.

cards.question: Jesus says the disciples will be seized and persecuted, but not until after the earthquakes and signs from heaven.

cards.text: On account of His name, they'll be handed over to synagogues and prisons and brought before kings and governors. Friend, I get nervous when the oven timer BEEPS. These guys are getting KINGS.

cards.question: Being brought before kings and governors sounds like the worst day ever. What does Jesus call it?

answers.text: A chance to serve as witnesses
A sign the end has come

cards.text: So Jesus tells them to 'make up your mind not to worry beforehand how to defend yourselves.' No rehearsing comebacks, and friend, I have won a LOT of arguments in my head and exactly zero out loud.

cards.question: Why don't the disciples need to plan their defense ahead of time?

answers.text: Jesus will give them speech and wisdom
The kings will be on their side
No one will ask them anything

cards.text: Then Jesus tells the disciples they will be betrayed. And He says by whom.

cards.question: Who does Jesus say will betray the disciples?

answers.text: Their parents and relatives and friends

cards.text: Some of them will be put to death, and they'll be hated by everyone because of His name. Jesus doesn't hide a thing from them.

cards.question: Right after all that, Jesus tells the disciples that not even a hair of their head will perish.
Jesus tells the disciples how they will gain their souls. How?

cards.text: Patient endurance. Friend, I did YEARS in the back of a junk drawer, so I've got a black belt in waiting, and now Jesus turns to Jerusalem itself.

cards.question: What will tell the disciples that Jerusalem's desolation is near?

answers.text: A new star over the city

cards.question: When Jerusalem is surrounded by armies, Jesus says those in Judea should flee to the ___.
When Jerusalem is surrounded by armies, Jesus tells the people out in the country to come into the city for safety.

cards.text: Jesus gives those days a name. He calls them the days of vengeance.

cards.question: Jesus calls the days when Jerusalem is surrounded the days of vengeance. What does He say they are for?

answers.text: To fulfill all that is written
To make the temple new again
To crown a new king there

cards.text: Then Jesus says, 'How miserable those days will be for pregnant and nursing mothers!' There will be great distress upon the land and wrath against this people.

cards.question: Jesus goes on about the people of Jerusalem: They will fall by the edge of the ___ and be led ___ into all the nations.
Jesus says Jerusalem will be trodden down by the Gentiles forever.

cards.text: Keep that apron on, friend. Jesus has more to say, and we're not leaving the bakery until we hear it.

findings.problem: "spear" is offered for the first blank ("fall by the edge of the ___"). Falling by the spear means nearly the same thing as falling by the sword: being killed by a weapon in the attack. A baker could argue it is right. The other two wrong words, "home" and "safely," don't fit the first blank at all. So the near-match "spear" is the only real competition for "sword," and the blank turns into a coin flip between two weapons rather than a test of meaning.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The last story card holds only the line saying the story isn't over, as allowed when the passage's last verse was asked on a choice card. It cites "Luke 21:24," but it tells nothing from that verse. The citation rule says a story card cites exactly the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last.
findings.question: When the last story card is only the story-isn't-over line and tells no verse content, what should its "verses" field cite? The last verse of the passage, the passage's full range, or nothing (null)?
